draft.title: Costs and benefits of globalisation
card: Benefits
Globalisation can bring cheaper goods, because firms can make or buy things where costs are lowest. It can also give firms bigger markets to sell to and create new jobs.
Costs
It can also cost some local jobs, when a business closes because imports or overseas production are cheaper. It may widen inequality, because the gains do not reach everyone equally.
Shocks
Economies that are closely linked can pass problems to each other. A downturn or a crisis in one country can spread to others through trade and money flows.
The effects differ between people. A shopper may gain from cheaper goods while a worker in a local factory loses a job.
draft.remember: Globalisation can bring cheaper goods, bigger markets and new jobs, but it can also cost local jobs, widen inequality and spread shocks.

a.q: Which is a cost of globalisation, not a benefit?
opts: A downturn in one country spreads to others
Shoppers can buy cheaper goods
Firms can sell to bigger markets
New jobs are created in export industries
a.why: Closely linked economies can pass shocks to each other, so a problem in one country can spread. The other three are benefits that the card lists.
a.clue: Which one is a problem that moves between countries?

b.q: A shoe factory in Ballarat closes because cheaper shoes are now imported. Shoppers in Ballarat pay less for shoes. What does this show?
opts: Globalisation can help some people and cost others
Globalisation only harms workers in every industry
Globalisation always makes goods cheaper and jobs safer
Globalisation helps workers but not shoppers
b.why: Shoppers gain from cheaper goods, while the factory workers lose their jobs. So the effects differ between groups. The wrong options say always or only, but the card says globalisation can have these effects.
b.clue: Look at what happens to the shoppers and to the workers.

a.best: A downturn in one country spreads to others

b.best: Globalisation can help some people and cost others

card: Benefits
Globalisation can bring cheaper goods, because firms can make or buy things where costs are lowest. It can also give firms bigger markets to sell to and create new jobs.
Costs
It can also cost some local jobs, when a business closes because imports or overseas production are cheaper. It may widen inequality, because the gains do not reach everyone equally.

proposal.remember: Globalisation can bring cheaper goods, bigger markets and new jobs, but it can also cost local jobs, widen inequality and spread shocks.

a.q: Which is a cost of globalisation, not a benefit?
opts: A downturn in one country spreads to others
Shoppers can buy cheaper goods
Firms can sell to bigger markets
New jobs are created in export industries
a.why: Closely linked economies can pass shocks to each other, so a downturn in one country can spread and leave others worse off. Bigger markets may sound like it involves other countries too, but it helps firms sell more, so it is a benefit.
a.clue: Think about which effect leaves people worse off.

b.q: A shoe factory in Ballarat closes because cheaper shoes are now imported. Shoppers in Ballarat pay less for shoes. Which effects of globalisation does this show?
opts: Cheaper goods and a loss of local jobs
Bigger markets and a loss of local jobs
Cheaper goods and new jobs in export firms
Bigger markets and new jobs in export firms
b.why: Shoppers paying less for shoes is the benefit of cheaper goods, and the factory closing is the cost of lost local jobs. Bigger markets is tempting, but that would mean a Ballarat firm selling more overseas, which does not happen here.
b.clue: Match the shoppers to one effect and the factory workers to another.

a.best: A downturn in one country spreads to others

b.best: Cheaper goods and a loss of local jobs
